# Joshua 21:1–22: Research notes

**What I could and couldn't find.** I ran out of searches before I could read the NET Bible notes, OCA (Orthodox) pages, or catholic.com, so none of those appear below. I found nothing from a Pentecostal, Wesleyan-holiness, or word-of-faith source that comments on these verses specifically. The one real disagreement between traditions is about the Levites' cities, and it shows up at vv. 1–2 and v. 12. Some of it comes to us secondhand, because the Pulpit Commentary reports what Calvin and Keil said.

---

**vv. 1–2: The Levites ask at Shiloh**

- **Who came.** The "fathers" of the Levites were Kohath, Gershon and Merari. The "heads" were the leading men then alive in each of those families. The fathers of the Levites were Kohath, Gershom, and Merari, and the heads of these were the chief persons now alive of these several families. (Benson/Poole on Biblehub) https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/21-1.htm
- **Why ask now.** Gill says the Levites made their claim once every tribe knew which cities it held and the six cities of refuge had been fixed. They had no share of the land but still needed somewhere to live. Shiloh was where the tabernacle stood. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html
- **Waiting their turn.** Matthew Henry (Presbyterian) says the Levites based their claim on God's command, not on what they deserved. He also praises their patience in being willing to be served last. it is also an instance of their humility, modesty, and patience … that they were willing to be served last, and they fared never the worse for it. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_021.cfm
- **Applying it to ministers.** Henry says paying ministers is not left to the people's goodwill, pointing to 1 Corinthians 9:14 (those who preach the gospel should live of the gospel). https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_021.cfm Benson (Methodist) repeats the point at v. 2. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/rbc/joshua-21.html
- **The curse that became a blessing.** Jacob had said Levi would be scattered (Gen 49:5–7). The Cambridge Bible notes that "the curse was with them turned into a blessing." https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/21-1.htm Guzik makes the same point: Levi was scattered "in a blessed sense," spreading their influence as priests and teachers. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-21/
- **Why the cities were needed.** Guzik says the cities were a safeguard: the Levites would still be supported even if Israel stopped tithing. https://enduringword.com/bible-commentary/joshua-21/
- **Where the traditions differ: had the Levites been forgotten?**
  - *Calvin (Reformed), as reported by others:* Calvin apparently thought the Levites had been overlooked until they spoke up. The Pulpit Commentary (Anglican) rejects this. It says the delay happened because the Levites' cities had to come out of the other tribes' land, so those tribes had to be settled first. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm
  - *Keil and Delitzsch (Lutheran)* also say Calvin's conclusion doesn't follow from the text. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/joshua/21-1.htm
  - At v. 2, the Pulpit says Calvin also complained that this account belonged before chapter 20. The Pulpit replies that Numbers 35 orders the cities of refuge to be chosen first. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm
- **Eleazar named first.** The Pulpit says that in a church matter the church leader came before the civil one. It also says Joshua consistently consulted the high priest after the Gibeonite mistake. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm
- **A word-of-faith comparison.** Precept Austin says the Levites' formal request is an example of legitimate "name it, claim it" theology, unlike much of what is taught today, because they were claiming something God had actually commanded. https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/62613/

**v. 3: Israel gives willingly**

- Adam Clarke (Methodist) says the tribes cheerfully obeyed the Divine command. The cities were assigned by lot to show that God chose where the Levites lived, just as he chose the other tribes' land. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/joshua-21.html
- Gill (Baptist) says the tribes raised no objection. They agreed among themselves which cities to give, and then lots decided which Levite family got which cities. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html
- Precept Austin notes there is no record of any tribe grumbling about giving. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-21-commentary
- The Pulpit notes that 48 is four times twelve and passes on Bähr's symbolic reading, which links it to the twelve-gated New Jerusalem of Revelation 21. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm
- **Catholic view.** The Catholic Encyclopedia says the cities came on top of the tithes and other dues Moses had already granted. It describes them as four cities from each tribe, 48 in all. https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/09206a.htm

**v. 4: The first lot goes to the priests**

- **Why use a lot.** The Pulpit says leaving the choice to God meant the division wouldn't later cause jealousy. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm
- **God's foresight.** Gill says God's providence placed the priests' cities in the tribes nearest Jerusalem, where the temple would later stand. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html The Pulpit says even Calvin remarked on God's foreknowledge here. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm Henry and Precept Austin say much the same. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_021.cfm https://www.preceptaustin.org/pdf/62613/
- **Why the priests went first.** The Pulpit says it was not because Kohath was the eldest son (Gershon appears to have been). It was because the priesthood belonged to Aaron's line. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm
- **Why so many cities.** Clarke says Judah, Simeon and Benjamin gave more because they held more land (Num 35:8). https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/joshua-21.html
- **Moses' humility.** The Pulpit says Moses never tried to "found a family." His descendants simply blended in with the ordinary Levites. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm
- **A critical objection and a reply.** Maurer and others argued that thirteen cities were far too many for Aaron's descendants. The Pulpit answers that:
  - the priests were not the only people living there;
  - their numbers grew fast;
  - many of the cities had not yet been taken;
  - the cities were small.

  The Pulpit also notes that Nob, a later priestly town, is missing from the list. It takes this as a sign that Joshua was written before Saul's reign. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm

**v. 5: The other Kohathites**

- Gill says these were Kohath's descendants through Izhar, Hebron and Uzziel. They were Levites but not priests, and their cities lay in the tribes next to the priests' cities. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html
- Henry says Moses' descendants were among them, and that Aaron's father's family settled nearest to Aaron's sons. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_021.cfm

**vv. 6–7: Gershon and Merari**

- Gill says the Gershonites (from Gershon, Levi's eldest son) got cities farther away, including in Bashan, east of the Jordan. The Merarites, from Levi's third son, got cities in Reuben and Gad across the Jordan and in Zebulun. That gives 48 in all (Num 35:7). https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html

**v. 8: Done as commanded**

- Gill says the pasturelands reached 2,000 cubits from each city. Spreading the cities among the tribes fulfilled Genesis 49:7 and let the Levites teach God's law everywhere. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html
- Henry says the 48 cities were first split into four groups of neighbouring cities, and lots then gave each group to a Levite family. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_021.cfm
- Precept Austin points out that v. 3 says the tribes gave freely, while v. 8 says the cities were assigned "by lot." https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-21-commentary

**vv. 9–10: "The first lot was theirs"**

- Gill says Simeon is paired with Judah because Simeon's cities lay inside Judah. As priests from Aaron's line, they had the honour of the first lot. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html
- The Jamieson-Fausset-Brown commentary sees God's wisdom in placing the priests' cities in Judah and Benjamin. This proved its worth when the kingdom split under Rehoboam. https://www.studylight.org/commentaries/eng/jfb/joshua-21.html

**v. 11: Kiriath-arba / Hebron**

- Gill passes on Kimchi's view that "Anak" may be a group name for the race of giants, with Arba as their chief. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html
- The Pulpit notes that the Hebrew word translated "hill country" is "mountain," the usual term for Palestine's highlands. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm
- Henry and Clarke both point out that David later began his reign at Hebron. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_021.cfm https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/joshua-21.html

**v. 12: Caleb keeps the fields**

- Gill says the Levites got the city and the land 2,000 cubits around it. Caleb kept the fields and villages beyond that. Gill says the same pattern held for every Levitical city. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html
- **Where the traditions differ: what did the Levites actually own?**
  - *Keil (Lutheran), as reported by the Pulpit:* the Levites got only as many houses as they needed, and Caleb kept the rest.
  - *Pulpit (Anglican):* agrees with Bähr that the Levites lived alongside the other residents and had pasture set aside for them. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm
  - *Clarke (Methodist):* the Levites probably did not own the cities outright, since other Israelites clearly lived there too. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/acc/joshua-21.html
  - *Henry (Presbyterian):* goes the other way. He says the Levites held the cities as lords and proprietors, not as tenants. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_021.cfm

**v. 13: Hebron, the city of refuge, and Libnah**

- The Pulpit says the better reading is "the city of refuge … Hebron." This shows the refuge cities were chosen first and then given to the Levites. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm
- Gill identifies Libnah as a royal city (Josh 10:29). https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html

**vv. 14–16: Jattir to Beth-shemesh**

- The Pulpit notes that 1 Chronicles 6:59 has "Ashan" instead of "Ain" and may be the correct reading. https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm
- Gill links Beth-shemesh with the town the ark was sent to (1 Sam 6). He also says the name ("house of the sun") points to an earlier sun temple there. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html

**vv. 17–18: Benjamin's four cities**

- Gill says Gibeon is the city the Gibeonites came from. Anathoth was Jeremiah's hometown, and Almon is the "Alemeth" of 1 Chronicles 6:60. Four cities was a lot for small Benjamin to give. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html
- The Pulpit says Anathoth was still a priestly town in Jeremiah's day, which is likely why Abiathar was banished there (1 Kings 2:26). https://biblehub.com/commentaries/pulpit/joshua/21.htm

**v. 19: Thirteen cities for the priests**

- Gill confirms that thirteen cities are named. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html

**v. 20: The rest of the Kohathites**

- Gill says these were the non-priestly Kohathites, including Moses' descendants according to the Jewish commentator Rashi ("Jarchi" in Gill). https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html

**vv. 21–22: Shechem, Gezer, Kibzaim, Beth-horon**

- Gill says Shechem's position on a mountain made it easy to see, which suited a city of refuge. He notes that the Canaanites were never driven out of Gezer. He identifies Kibzaim with "Jokmeam" in 1 Chronicles 6:68 and says Beth-horon means Upper Beth-horon. https://studylight.org/commentaries/eng/geb/joshua-21.html
- Henry notes that Abimelech, the first Israelite to call himself king, later ruled in Shechem. https://www.blueletterbible.org/Comm/mhc/Jos/Jos_021.cfm

---

**Other views on the whole passage**

- **Modern scholarship.** Bible Odyssey says that in Deuteronomy the Levites make up the whole priesthood and live in towns across the country, perhaps in special levitical cities (Josh 21:1-42). It adds that later the Jerusalem authorities pushed them into a lower role. https://bibleodyssey.org/glossary/levites
- **When was the list written?** Utley, quoted on Precept Austin, says some of the 48 cities were not under Israelite control until the monarchy. That suggests at least parts of the list come from later than Joshua. https://www.preceptaustin.org/joshua-21-commentary
- **A sceptical view.** The ISBE entry on Biblehub reports an unnamed critic who argues that "there is not a historical trace of the existence of the Levitical cities." https://biblehub.com/topical/l/levitical_cities.htm
- **Catholic view.** The Catholic Encyclopedia notes that thirteen of the 48 towns went to the priests. https://www.newadvent.org/cathen/12409a.htm
